key_insight: Higher-gradient regularization enables an existence proof for finite-strain elastoplastic evolution, while vectorized FEM makes the logarithmic-strain framework computationally practical.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports simulations of elastoplastic solids undergoing large rotations and deformations without substantially increasing computational costs in the reported benchmarks.
method: Use logarithmic strains with von Mises plasticity and linear kinematic hardening.
Introduce higher-gradient regularization and prove existence of energetic solutions under time-dependent Dirichlet loading.
Vectorize MATLAB FEM using page-wise matrix functions and a custom vectorization library.
evidence_signal: Computational benchmarks report significantly faster local tensor operations and robust handling of large rotations and deformations, but the abstract provides no numerical speedup factors.
watch_item: The existence result relies on higher-gradient regularization; its parameter choice and discretization require care in practical applications.
paper_title: Mathematical analysis and vectorized FEM implementation of logarithmic strain space framework for finite strains: a case study on elastoplasticity
